title: Rakos_Backdoor_Investigation_bcf
description: Investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Rakos backdoor malware. This malware spreads via brute force SSH attacks and establishes command-and-control (C2) communication. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's activities, and contain the threat. This training will teach you how to identify and mitigate such threats using various tools and techniques.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:

- Password: cyrano

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content:
Investigate the target host for any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target host? The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all services. Look for any services that appear unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service in this scenario is `javaxxx.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the concept of systemd services and how they can be used to maintain persistence on a system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services running on the system.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that you did not install. The suspicious service in this scenario is `javaxxx.service`.

levels.title: Determine Service Persistence
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd service unit file responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, examine the systemd service files using the `systemctl status javaxxx.service` command. The service unit file responsible for the persistence is `javaxxx.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how systemd service unit files can be used to maintain persistence on a system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status javaxxx.service` to check the status of the suspicious service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for the service unit file that starts the suspicious service automatically. The service unit file responsible for the persistence is `javaxxx.service`.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement
levels.content:
Identify file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.

**Question:** What is the name of the service responsible for transferring files from the target host to the next-target host? The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: To identify the lateral movement mechanism, investigate the systemd services using the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command. The service responsible for transferring files is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how lateral movement can be achieved through file transfers or remote execution.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services running on the system.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for services with names that suggest file transfer or remote execution. The service responsible for transferring files is `payload-transfer.service`.
